title: The Bramblebell Moot
theme: Enchanted forest village of talking paths, hidden bargains, and fey-lit cottages
hook: A forest village that should have hosted the spring moot has vanished behind a curtain of singing leaves. The road still reaches its gate, but every traveler who enters returns with a different memory of what they promised inside.
background:
Bramblebell was once a meeting place where mortal villagers, forest spirits, and wandering folk settled disputes beneath the old moon-bough. Now the spring moot never begins: signs lie, paths loop, and guests leave with promises they do not remember making.

Three promise-tokens have been stolen from the moot table, and without them the village cannot tell fair bargains from tricks. The party must find the tokens, learn who is twisting the old customs, and ring the Bramblebell before the village forgets the outside world entirely.

layout.notes: Enchanted forest village with a central green, branching garden paths, cottage clusters, bridges, side shrines, and an upper moot hall.

rooms.name: Root-Gate Steps
rooms.readAloud: Stone steps climb between roots braided into an arch. Small bells hang from the branches, ringing different names for the same village.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the main entry. The bells greet honest arrivals warmly and repeat lies in a childlike voice.
rooms.treasure: A fallen bell of green bronze is tucked under the right root. It rings only when someone speaks a promise they mean to keep.
rooms.secrets: The bells know that three promise-tokens are missing, but they reveal this only if politely asked for the village by its old name.
rooms.exits: Up the root stair to Room 2, or along the lower left garden trail to Room 3.

rooms.name: Moon-Bough Green
rooms.readAloud: The village green opens beneath a vast silver-leafed tree. Paths, bridges, cottage walks, and carved thresholds radiate from a round moot table.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the social hub. The secret marker represents a hollow beneath the moot table where one promise-token was hidden by a frightened villager.

inhabitants.name: Nettlecap Speaker
inhabitants.tactics: Offers riddling bargains, calls nearby sprites for help, and tries to split impatient visitors from careful ones
inhabitants.morale: Cooperates if the party returns one promise-token or exposes the false signposts
inhabitants.wants: The moot restored without admitting the village elders made a mistake
inhabitants.leverage: Likes courtesy, music, public apologies, and anyone who refuses an obviously unfair bargain

rooms.treasure: A moon-bough leaf pressed under the table can be traded for safe lodging in friendly forest settlements.
rooms.secrets: A loose table root hides the first promise-token, marked with the word Welcome.

rooms.name: Candlecap Cottages
rooms.readAloud: A cluster of tiny cottages glows with mushroom lamps. Their doors are open, but the shadows inside move as if someone just ducked away.
rooms.gmNotes: This room favors investigation and conversation. The secret marker belongs to a cottage floorboard with scratched names underneath.
rooms.treasure: A packet of sleep-saffron tea, valuable to herbalists and dangerous if brewed too strong.
rooms.secrets: The scratched names identify who last touched the promise-token hidden under the moot table in Room 2.
rooms.exits: Trail to Room 2, lower garden trail to Room 1, and path through foxglove hedges to Room 4.

rooms.name: Foxglove Market Walk
rooms.readAloud: Empty stalls lean under purple flowers. Wooden price tags list impossible trades: one laugh, two secrets, a memory of rain.
rooms.gmNotes: Use this as a playful negotiation space. A fair trade at any stall makes the path to Room 5 easier to notice.

inhabitants.name: Foxglove Tally-Keeper
inhabitants.tactics: Marks unfair traders with glowing pollen and calls thorny vines if robbed
inhabitants.morale: Stays cheerful unless someone cheats a child, guest, or hungry creature
inhabitants.wants: Every trade named clearly and paid honestly
inhabitants.leverage: Accepts songs, apologies, useful rumors, or amusing but harmless objects

rooms.treasure: A jar of star-honey sits behind a stall labeled For brave apologies only.
rooms.secrets: One price tag is written in the same hand as the false signposts scattered through the village.
rooms.exits: Trail to Room 2, path to Room 3, and stepped garden walk to Room 5.

rooms.name: Sleepy Well Of Petals
rooms.readAloud: A round well is choked with pale petals. Each petal drifts upward instead of down, carrying whispered dreams out of the water.
rooms.gmNotes: This is a quiet hazard and clue room. Falling asleep near the well shows the route to one missing token, but leaves the dreamer vulnerable.
rooms.treasure: A silver drinking cup rests on the inner lip, etched with the village motto: Guests before grudges.
rooms.secrets: A dreamer sees promise-starlings in Room 11 repeating the exact words that can expose the false signs in Room 14.
rooms.exits: Stepped garden walk back to Room 4.

rooms.name: Whisper-Wood Yard
rooms.readAloud: Carved posts and low fences surround a yard where the trees whisper over each other. The path changes whenever no one is looking at it.
rooms.gmNotes: The party can calm the shifting paths by naming where they intend to go before moving.

inhabitants.name: Whisper-Wood Saplings
inhabitants.tactics: Move paths behind intruders, separate noisy groups, and tangle anyone who mocks the forest
inhabitants.morale: Settle if addressed as sentries rather than obstacles
inhabitants.leverage: They respect names, patient navigation, and repaired fence posts

rooms.treasure: A carved wayfinder peg points to the last place its holder spoke truthfully.
rooms.secrets: The trees know a shortcut to Room 9, but only reveal it after someone repairs a broken fence rail.
rooms.exits: Trail to Room 2, stair through roots to Room 7, and north trail to Room 9.

rooms.name: Acorn Tollhouse
rooms.readAloud: A miniature tollhouse sits between two roots. Its windows are bright, and a line of acorns waits politely outside the door.
rooms.gmNotes: The treasure marker belongs here. The tollhouse is guarded by etiquette, not locks.

inhabitants.name: Acorn Clerk
inhabitants.tactics: Stamps ankles, redirects rude guests, and calls birds to carry off shiny stolen things
inhabitants.morale: Very brave while inside the tollhouse, very sensible outside it
inhabitants.wants: One proper toll from every traveler
inhabitants.leverage: Accepts compliments, breadcrumbs, useful stamps, or a promise to return lost acorns

rooms.treasure: The toll chest contains a promise-token marked Fair Passage, plus a handful of pearl acorns.
rooms.secrets: The clerk saw a laughing shadow pass toward Room 8 after stealing the third token.
rooms.exits: Root stair back to Room 6, or trail along the old boundary hedge to Room 8.

rooms.name: Hollow Hedge Playhouse
rooms.readAloud: A hedge has grown into the shape of a little theater. Leaf masks hang over the stage, smiling too widely.
rooms.gmNotes: This area is playful until the party refuses to play any role. Then the masks become an active obstacle.

inhabitants.name: Leaf-Mask Players
inhabitants.tactics: Swap voices, force comic misunderstandings, and flee through the hedge when cornered
inhabitants.morale: Surrender if the party finishes a scene with kindness instead of force
inhabitants.wants: A performance that admits what the village is afraid to say
inhabitants.leverage: They cannot resist a sincere improvised apology

rooms.treasure: One mask becomes a harmless disguise if its role is played to a fair ending.
rooms.secrets: The laughing shadow hid behind the mayor role and carried the third promise-token toward the east orchard.
rooms.exits: Boundary hedge trail back to Room 7.

rooms.name: Lantern-Moss Garden
rooms.readAloud: Blue-green moss lanterns float above a stepping path. Their light gathers in pools that show places the viewer has promised to visit.
rooms.gmNotes: This is a strong clue room and a visual crossroads between the west paths and the upper hall.
rooms.treasure: A moss lantern can be coaxed into a covered jar; it shines toward broken promises.
rooms.secrets: The garden reveals the raised root bridge and worn trail both lead back to the Moon-Bough Green in Room 2.
rooms.exits: Raised root bridge and worn garden trail to Room 2, trail to Room 6, and bridge to Room 10.

rooms.name: Elderleaf Hall
rooms.readAloud: A long hall of living branches forms a green roof overhead. Benches have grown from the floor, each bearing a different family mark.
rooms.gmNotes: The village elders are absent, but their old judgments are recorded in the bench marks.

inhabitants.name: Benchmark Echoes
inhabitants.tactics: Ask loaded questions, close branch doors, and repeat any contradiction
inhabitants.morale: Fade after a fair judgment is spoken aloud
inhabitants.wants: The moot restored through truth rather than victory
inhabitants.leverage: They must honor balanced testimony from at least two sides

rooms.treasure: A family mark carved from amber is loose beneath the central bench.
rooms.secrets: The elders once hid promises to avoid offending the forest spirits; the current crisis began as a cover-up.
rooms.exits: Corridor-threshold to Room 2, bridge to Room 9, and stair up through the branches to Room 11.

rooms.name: Starling Roost
rooms.readAloud: The upper branches open into a roost of woven twigs and colored thread. Starlings repeat overheard promises in dozens of bright voices.
rooms.gmNotes: The secret marker belongs here. The birds know the exact words needed to expose the false signs, but they will not help anyone who grabs at the nest.

inhabitants.name: Promise-Starlings
inhabitants.tactics: Mob thieves, shout embarrassing truths, and scatter clues to safer listeners
inhabitants.morale: Keep their distance unless offered bright thread or patient questions
inhabitants.leverage: They trade information for colorful thread, seed, or a funny true story

rooms.treasure: The nest holds several beads of sky-blue glass and a ribbon that never knots when tied honestly.
rooms.secrets: A starling can repeat the exact words needed to silence the false signs near Room 14.

rooms.name: Sunberry Apiary
rooms.readAloud: Golden hives hang from bent trees. Bees the size of thumbs drift between flowers, each leaving a thread of warm light behind it.
rooms.gmNotes: The treasure marker belongs here. The bees are not hostile unless someone smokes, swats, or steals without asking.

inhabitants.name: Sunberry Bees
inhabitants.tactics: Drive intruders toward thorny brush, swarm exposed hands, and ignore anyone carrying flowers calmly
inhabitants.morale: Return to the hives once their queen is safe
inhabitants.wants: The hives kept whole and the orchard unburned
inhabitants.leverage: They accept pollen offerings, slow movement, and songs in a low voice

rooms.treasure: A comb of sunberry honey glows warmly and can calm frightened forest creatures.
rooms.secrets: Honey poured onto a false sign makes the lie run off like ink.

rooms.name: Moonroot Pantry
rooms.readAloud: A crooked pantry leans over a patch of pale roots. Clay jars hum softly, and every shelf smells like a different season.
rooms.gmNotes: The treasure marker belongs here. The best treasure is useful at the table rather than raw wealth.
rooms.treasure: Three moonroot loaves, one jar of winter jam, and a spoon that points toward the nearest honest meal.
rooms.secrets: A pantry shelf bears the same false handwriting seen in Room 4, proving someone forged the village bargains.

structuredExits.label: Route to Room 14
structuredExits.description: Pantry path to Room 14.

rooms.name: Orchard Bridge Yard
rooms.readAloud: A bridge yard spans a bright stream between fruit trees. Half the fruit is ripe, half is carved from painted wood, and both halves sway in the same wind.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the east-side junction. The false signposts here try to send the party in circles unless contradicted with the starlings' exact words from Room 11.

inhabitants.name: Painted-Fruit Imps
inhabitants.tactics: Throw wooden fruit, swap signs, and lure pursuers toward the stream bridge
inhabitants.morale: Scatter if one of their false signs is publicly corrected
inhabitants.wants: Keep the moot confused so nobody asks who stole the tokens
inhabitants.leverage: They brag under pressure and fear the promise-starlings in Room 11

rooms.treasure: A wooden pear opens to reveal the third promise-token marked Good Guest.
rooms.secrets: The imps were hired by a laughing shadow that cannot cross the stream unless invited by name.
rooms.exits: Bridge to Room 2, garden trail to Room 12, pantry path to Room 13, and bridge to Room 15.

rooms.name: Bellflower Watch
rooms.readAloud: A raised watch platform looks back over the whole village. Bellflowers grow along the rail, their petals shaped like tiny ringing mouths.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the best finale room if the party has recovered the three promise-tokens. Ringing the Bramblebell from here ends the village loop.

inhabitants.name: Laughing Shadow
inhabitants.tactics: Uses stolen voices, flees across bridges, and turns promises against anyone who speaks carelessly
inhabitants.morale: Runs if all three promise-tokens are set into the bell frame
inhabitants.wants: Keep Bramblebell entertaining, forgetful, and unable to hold a true moot
inhabitants.leverage: It cannot refuse a clearly worded bargain witnessed by the whole village

rooms.treasure: Restoring the Bramblebell earns the party a village favor and a bellflower charm that rings near broken bargains.
rooms.secrets: The shadow was first invited by an elder who wanted one embarrassing promise forgotten.

Promise-token marked Welcome from beneath the moot table

gmNotes: Lean into exploration and social play first; most inhabitants prefer bargains, jokes, or public honesty before violence.
The three key tokens are hidden in Rooms 2, 7, and 14. Room 11 provides the exact words needed to expose the false signs without a fight.
The laughing shadow is dangerous because it steals exact wording, not because it is stronger than the whole village.
If the party restores the Bramblebell from Room 15, the village becomes safe passage and a recurring ally.
